plain.li: I went into the storeroom to count the food and finished counting much too quickly. We need a month's worth, at least.
[fall] The fields have a few weeks left in them. Whatever we don't put away now, we'll be wishing for in winter.

warm.li: I never want to cut anyone's portion in half again. Let's store what we can while the fields still give it.

blunt.li: Empty shelves make people stupid and mean. Fill them.

cheerful.li: Sacks in every corner, and a pantry so full you have to squeeze in sideways!

gloomy.li: I expect every colony that starved thought it had enough put away.

cold.li: Hunger is the one threat we can predict to the day. I've done the count, and we're short.

plain.li: The storeroom door doesn't shut properly anymore. There are too many sacks behind it.

warm.li: Every bowl gets filled this season, and I'll sleep better for it.

gloomy.li: A month of food put by. I still dream about empty shelves.

plain.li: I've thrown out more spoiled meat this month than we ate. A cold room with thirty meals in it, and that stops.

warm.li: I'd like to cook a big batch on a good day and know it'll still be good for you next week.

blunt.li: The flies are eating better than we are. Cold room, now.

cheerful.li: You open the door, a cloud of cold air rolls out, and behind it there's dinner.

gloomy.li: Rotten food makes people sick, and out here sick people die. I'd rather keep it cold.

cold.li: Every spoiled meal is a cook's afternoon thrown away.

plain.li: Thirty meals on the shelves and frost on the walls. I checked the door twice.

cheerful.li: I stood in there for a minute just to feel the cold on my face!

cold.li: Spoilage is now negligible.

plain.li: Last raid I was stitching someone up on the dining table, between the salt and the bread. We need real beds for this.
[afterraid] Count the bandages we used this week. Now count what's left. That's why I'm asking for a hospital.

warm.li: When one of us gets hurt, they should wake up somewhere clean. Someone should be watching over them.

blunt.li: I'm tired of doing surgery on a dirty floor. Someone has to hold the lamp and someone has to hold the patient.

cheerful.li: Clean sheets on three beds and a whole shelf of medicine! It'll be the nicest room in the colony.

gloomy.li: Everyone ends up on a sickbed sooner or later. Mine should at least be clean.

cold.li: Infection has killed more of our wounded than the wounds did. I've kept count.

plain.li: I've sorted the medicine by kind and put a clean sheet on every bed.

warm.li: Whoever's next in one of these beds, I hope it's only for a scratch.

cold.li: Three beds and fifteen doses. I'll be keeping track of who uses them most.

plain.li: I haven't been alone with my own thoughts since I got here. Rooms. One each.

warm.li: Some of us cry at night and try to do it without a sound. A room each would spare them that.

blunt.li: I know what every one of you sounds like asleep. I'd like to forget. Build walls.

cheerful.li: A room of my own, where I could sing in bed and not get a boot thrown at me.

gloomy.li: There's no privacy in a barracks, not even for grief. I'd like a door to close when it's bad.

cold.li: One cough in the barracks last month became four by the end of the week. Separate the beds.

plain.li: I closed my door last night just to hear it click.

blunt.li: Now knock before you come in. All of you.

gloomy.li: My own room. It's very quiet in there, and that takes some getting used to.

plain.li: We eat together every day. Let's do it somewhere that makes us want to stay at the table.

warm.li: I want a room where we toast the good days and sit together through the bad ones.

blunt.li: Visitors walk in, look at our dining room, and pity us. I can see it on their faces.

cheerful.li: Candles down a long table and a painting worth staring at. We'd eat like lords!

gloomy.li: We've eaten too many funeral suppers in that cramped little room. The next one deserves better.

cold.li: Guests judge us by where we feed them. Let them leave thinking we're stronger than we are.

plain.li: Look at it. You walk in here and you sit up straighter.

blunt.li: Nobody eats with their hands in here. I mean it.

cheerful.li: I've eaten three meals in here today. I'm thinking about a fourth, just to sit in it a while longer.

plain.li: I've played the same game of horseshoes so many times I've started losing on purpose. We need more to do.

warm.li: There are people here who haven't laughed in weeks. A room for games would help more than you'd think.

blunt.li: Bored people break things, and sometimes each other.

cheerful.li: I'll run tournaments, and the winner gets the first helping at supper.

gloomy.li: The days run together here. Work, eat, sleep, and then the same again.

cold.li: Bored colonists make trouble. Give them something harmless to do.

plain.li: Five ways to waste an evening, all under one roof.

cheerful.li: I lost every single game tonight and had the best time of my life!

gloomy.li: I won a game today. First thing I've won in a long time.

plain.li: Last time they came, I was shooting from behind the firewood pile. Let's build some real cover.
[afterraid] We counted the holes in the walls this morning, then we stopped counting. We need better defenses.

warm.li: I keep thinking about who we'd lose if they hit us harder. I don't like the names I come up with.

blunt.li: Next raid, I want to be behind something solid, looking down a long empty field at them.

cheerful.li: Barricades on every approach and a nice clear line of fire. It'll be like a real fort!

gloomy.li: The raids only get bigger. One day they'll be big enough. I'd like that day to come later.

cold.li: I've walked our approaches the way a raider would. I didn't find much to stop me.

warm.li: I walked the whole line, and for once I think we could protect each other.

cold.li: Our position is sound. I've written down where each of you will stand.

plain.li: Three turrets on the approaches would see raiders coming before any of us did.

warm.li: Turrets can take the first hits, so the rest of us don't have to.

blunt.li: I'm tired of being the one who stands in the open. Let a machine do it.

cheerful.li: Three turrets on the approaches, and finally a full night's sleep for whoever's on watch!

gloomy.li: A turret doesn't freeze up when the shooting starts. Some of us do.

cold.li: A turret costs less than a colonist and complains less.

plain.li: Turrets are up. Keep out of their line of fire when it starts.

gloomy.li: They'll blow up one day. I've marked where not to stand when they do.

plain.li: Six traps where the raiders like to walk. They'll be limping before they ever see our walls.
[lowtech] Sharpened stakes in the long grass. My grandmother's people did it, and they were raided less than most.

warm.li: Every raider a trap stops is one I don't have to shoot. I'd like to shoot fewer people.

blunt.li: I want the walk to our door to be the worst walk of their lives.

cheerful.li: Hidden, pointy and sneaky, every one of them. We'll just have to remember where they are.

gloomy.li: They'll get through eventually. Let's make sure fewer of them do.

cold.li: A raider with a spike through the foot has to be carried home by two others. I like those numbers.

plain.li: Traps are set. Learn the safe path, all of you.

blunt.li: Now we wait for someone to come the wrong way.

gloomy.li: Someone's going to forget and step on one. Just don't let it be me.

plain.li: The lights went out twice during supper last week. Two batteries would carry us through.

warm.li: I don't want anyone on the operating table when the power cuts out.

blunt.li: I'm sick of eating dinner in the dark because the wind dropped.

cheerful.li: Two little boxes full of lightning, humming away in the corner. I love that.

gloomy.li: When the heaters stop at night, you find out how thin the walls really are.

cold.li: I've timed the blackouts. We lose an hour of work in each, and the freezer creeps up a few degrees.

plain.li: Batteries are full and humming. I checked them three times before bed.

gloomy.li: Now when the lights go out, it'll be because something worse happened.

cold.li: The batteries carried us to sunrise with a third left over. That will do.

plain.li: Right now I sew clothes on a bench in the hallway. Give me a real workshop and watch what comes out of it.

warm.li: With a proper workshop, I could mend things before they turn to rags.

blunt.li: I can't make good things in a bad room.

cheerful.li: A workshop with the tools hung on the wall, each in its own painted outline. I've dreamed about the outlines.

gloomy.li: Our gear is held together with string, and it won't hold through another season.

cold.li: Our gear wears out faster than we replace it. I can tell you roughly when we'll run out.

plain.li: Two stations, good light, a door that shuts. I could work in here forever.

blunt.li: Don't touch my tools.

cheerful.li: The first thing out of the new workshop is a spoon. It's not a very good spoon, but there'll be more.

plain.li: We look at bare walls all day. I want to look at something someone made on purpose, just because it was beautiful.

warm.li: A sculpture where we eat would give us something to talk about besides raids.

blunt.li: Bare walls everywhere you look. Give me a block of stone and leave me alone for a week.

cheerful.li: Three pieces of art, and one of them should be a statue of the cook!

gloomy.li: Someday people will dig this place up. I want them to find more than bones.

cold.li: People are calmer in pleasant rooms, and calm people make fewer mistakes.

plain.li: Someone just stood in front of one of them for five minutes without saying a word.

blunt.li: Don't hang your coats on the sculptures.

cheerful.li: I've started calling the dining room the gallery, and it's catching on.

plain.li: I've watched the same herd graze past the fields all week. Three of them could be ours.

warm.li: An animal doesn't care what kind of day you've had. I think we could all use that.

blunt.li: Animals haul and never complain, which is more than I can say for some of you.

cheerful.li: At least one fluffy one, please, and one with a silly face.

gloomy.li: Animals are always glad to see you in the morning. People here aren't.

cold.li: Three animals, minimum. If one doesn't take to us, it still has meat on it.

plain.li: Three new animals and a barn for them. It smells like a farm in there, and I like it.

warm.li: They followed me in from the field today. I think they've decided we're family.

cold.li: Three animals tamed. I've put their names on the feeding rota.

plain.li: There's so much we don't know how to make yet, and we keep paying traders for it instead.

warm.li: Every project we finish is something nobody here has to struggle with again.

blunt.li: Everything here gets done the hard way because no one's had time to learn an easier one.

cheerful.li: A lab with notes pinned on every wall and a pot of tea that never goes cold. I can't wait.

gloomy.li: The raiders turn up with better weapons every year. Ours are the ones we started with.

cold.li: A finished project keeps paying off for as long as the colony stands. Few things we buy do that.

plain.li: Three projects done. My head hurts in the good way.

cheerful.li: I learned three whole things, and I'm going to explain all of them at dinner!

gloomy.li: The more I learn, the more I see how close we came to not making it.

plain.li: Every winter we watch the fields die and start counting the days until the thaw.

warm.li: Think of bringing a bowl of fresh greens to whoever's sick in midwinter.
[winter] Look outside. Nothing's growing. Now imagine walking into a warm room full of green.

blunt.li: The weather's been deciding whether we eat for too long. Let's take its vote away.

cheerful.li: Strawberries in winter! I'm eating the first one myself.

gloomy.li: One cold snap at the wrong time and the whole harvest is gone. I've seen it happen.

cold.li: Outdoor farming is a gamble with bad odds, and we've lost it before.

plain.li: The first seedlings are up under the lamps.

warm.li: Come and stand in here for a minute. It's the best-smelling room in the colony.

cold.li: Winter used to decide how much we ate. Now I do.

plain.li: I slept in my coat most of last winter. Let's put heat in the bedrooms this time.
[fall] The nights are getting colder already. Let's get heat into every bedroom before the first frost.

warm.li: This winter, everyone should wake up with feeling in their fingers.

blunt.li: I'm not freezing in my bed so we can save on firewood.

cheerful.li: Imagine waking up warm, without your breath frozen to the blanket.

gloomy.li: I've seen people go to sleep cold and not wake up. I'd rather not see it again.

cold.li: A colonist who sleeps cold works slowly the next day. I watched it happen all last winter.

plain.li: I slept with my arms outside the blanket last night. That's how warm it is.

cheerful.li: I'm going to sleep with my socks off tonight!

gloomy.li: Warm rooms. I'll believe it when it's snowing sideways and I still can't see my breath.

plain.li: The beds in the barracks are half empty and the work isn't.
[small] There are so few of us that one bad fever would empty the fields. We need more people.

warm.li: We've got a spare bed and food enough for one more. Someone out there needs both.

blunt.li: I don't care if it's a refugee or a prisoner who's changed their mind. We need hands.

cheerful.li: A new face, with new stories, who hasn't heard all my jokes yet!

gloomy.li: Every time we lose someone, there are fewer of us to dig the next grave. Let's grow instead.

cold.li: One bad week and there aren't enough of us to keep both the fields and the walls. Recruit.

plain.li: The new arrival's settling in. Somebody show them where we keep the good meals.

cheerful.li: The new one laughed at my joke!

cold.li: One more pair of hands. I'll find out what they're good for.

plain.li: I've seen more scowls this week than smiles. Whatever's wrong, let's find it and fix it.

warm.li: It's been weeks since I heard anyone laugh at supper.

blunt.li: I'm sick of everybody's moods, mine included. Let's sort it out before someone throws a punch.

cheerful.li: Let's make this the happiest place on the Rim, starting with a proper meal and a day off.

gloomy.li: I'd like to remember how this place felt when we first got here, before it got heavy.

cold.li: I've been keeping a note of who's close to breaking. The list is getting long.

plain.li: Somebody hummed at supper. I haven't heard that in a long time.

cheerful.li: I went round and asked every one of you. All happy. I wrote it down.

gloomy.li: Good moods all round. I keep waiting for the catch.

plain.li: The last caravan had everything we needed, and we couldn't pay for any of it. Let's put silver aside.

warm.li: One day that silver might pay a ransom for one of us. It should be there when we need it.

blunt.li: Traders can smell poverty. I want them to smell silver.

cheerful.li: A big pile of shiny silver. I'd just like to look at it sometimes.

gloomy.li: The day we need something desperately is the day the trader doubles the price. Let's be ready for it.

cold.li: Silver turns into medicine, weapons or a ransom the moment we need one of them.

plain.li: Two thousand silver put by. The next trader can name a price, and we'll name ours.

cheerful.li: I sat on the pile of silver, just for a moment!

cold.li: Our reserves are sufficient. From now on we negotiate from strength.

plain.li: Simple meals keep us alive. I want to cook something that makes people close their eyes when they eat it.

warm.li: Cooking well for someone is a way of saying you're glad they're here. Let me say it properly.

blunt.li: I can do a lot better than this slop if someone gives me a kitchen worth the name.

cheerful.li: Real sauces and seasoning, and meals with more than one color in them.

gloomy.li: Some nights a good meal is the only thing that goes right all day. I'd like more of those nights.

cold.li: A well-fed colonist is a patient colonist. We're short on patience here.

plain.li: Twenty fine meals and a kitchen I'm proud of. Come and get it.

blunt.li: Eat it slowly. I didn't cook it for you to inhale it.

cheerful.li: Somebody cried over their plate, the good kind of crying!

plain.li: The ones who fell sick last week all ate the same stew, and I've seen where it was made.

warm.li: The cooks work so hard. Let's give them a kitchen they don't have to scrub blood out of first.

blunt.li: There's a pile of guts on the floor next to the soup pot. Right now. Go and look.

cheerful.li: A kitchen so clean it squeaks, with the butchering done somewhere far away.

gloomy.li: We got through the last raid and then lost two days to bad stew.

cold.li: I've worked out how many days of work we lost to sickness last season. Most of it came out of one room.

plain.li: The kitchen smells of soap now. I'd forgotten it could.

blunt.li: Anybody who drags a carcass in here goes out with it.

cold.li: I've stopped counting the days we lose to bad stew. There aren't any.

plain.li: We keep leaving wounded raiders to die in the mud. A cell would let us turn a few of them into neighbors.
[afterraid] There's a raider out there who's still breathing. Right now our choices are a knife or leaving them. Let's build a third.

warm.li: Some of the people who attack us are just hungry and desperate. A bed behind a door would give them a way out.

blunt.li: I want somewhere to put the ones who shot at me, so I can watch them heal.

cheerful.li: A cell with a real bed and a blanket. We'll run the friendliest prison on the Rim!

gloomy.li: No one comes to the Rim because they want to. Some of the raiders just need a reason to stop fighting.

cold.li: A raider who dies in the mud is worth nothing to us. A raider in a cell is worth whatever we decide.

plain.li: The cell's ready. Strange thing to be proud of, but I am.

warm.li: I put a blanket on the prison bed. It's still a bed.

cold.li: The cell's done. I'll pick out who goes in it at the next raid.

plain.li: Traders charge a fortune for beer. We could make our own for the price of some hops and a bit of waiting.

warm.li: When we bury someone, I'd like there to be something to pour for them. Something we made.

blunt.li: Everyone's on edge. Beer won't fix that, but it'll help.

cheerful.li: A brewery, and a tasting committee. I volunteer for the committee.

gloomy.li: There's not much joy out here, and I'm tired of waiting for a trader to sell us some.

cold.li: People drink whether we brew it or not. If we brew it, at least we know what's in it.

plain.li: Twenty-five bottles on the shelf, saved for the next thing worth celebrating. One each tonight, though.

blunt.li: Drink what you like. Just don't throw up in the barrels.

gloomy.li: Now we have something to drink at the funerals.

plain.li: I counted the wooden walls on my way here this morning. I stopped at forty.

warm.li: We've put so much into these rooms. I can't stand the thought of watching them burn.

blunt.li: Wood walls are just firewood we've agreed to live inside.

cheerful.li: I've picked out the stone already. It has little sparkly bits in it.

gloomy.li: All it takes is one lightning strike, or one careless cook.

cold.li: Wooden walls need rebuilding after every fire. Stone doesn't.

plain.li: Stone, nearly all of it. I knocked on a wall today just to hear how solid it is.

cheerful.li: I held a torch to a wall to test it. It passed.

gloomy.li: Fireproof. Something else will have to kill us.

plain.li: After dark I can't tell the storeroom from the bedroom, and I've slept in the wrong one.

warm.li: I hate watching people feel their way to bed along the walls.

blunt.li: I tripped over someone asleep in the corridor, and they swung at me.

cheerful.li: No more dark corners, and no more guessing what I just stepped in.

gloomy.li: Things move in the dark corners. I'd rather see what they are.

cold.li: The dark is where the accidents happen. I'd rather they happened nowhere.

plain.li: Not a dark corner left. Found three things I'd lost, and one I wish I hadn't.

cheerful.li: I walked through every room and didn't stub a single toe!

gloomy.li: Now I can see how dirty everything is.

plain.li: One of these days it'll be a wound near the heart. Then the hands holding the needle will matter more than anything.

warm.li: I've watched someone die because none of us knew what to do. I want to know what to do.

blunt.li: Whoever stitched my arm last time did it like they were angry at it. Let someone actually learn.

cheerful.li: I'll practice my stitches on fruit first, then on volunteers.

gloomy.li: We've run out of medicine twice already. Next time, I want someone who can manage without it.

cold.li: A skilled surgeon turns a dead colonist into a merely injured one. That's a very good trade.

plain.li: We have someone who really knows what to do with a needle now. I sleep better.

cheerful.li: Our doctor's the real thing now! I'm first in line for a check-up.

cold.li: With a doctor this good, most wounds are just a few days off work.

plain.li: Everything we wear is patched and everything we fight with is chipped. Let someone get good enough to fix that properly.

warm.li: I want to make armor good enough that I never have to see one of you bleed through it.

blunt.li: The raiders' castoffs are better than what we make. That's embarrassing.

cheerful.li: A coat so fine that traders try to buy it off your back. That's what I'm aiming for.

gloomy.li: Bad gear fails in the middle of a fight. A strap snapped on me once, and I was lucky.

cold.li: One skilled crafter raises the value of every raw material we own.

plain.li: Made a coat today. Good stitching, good fit. Best thing I've ever made.

blunt.li: Ruin anything I made and I'll make you wear it anyway.

cheerful.li: Someone asked who made their armor, and I got to say it was me!

plain.li: Meat and vegetables, pressed and dried. Ugly food, but it'll still be good long after everything else has rotted.

warm.li: Anyone who has to travel should carry food that won't turn on the second day.

blunt.li: I don't care that it tastes of old leather. Make it.

cheerful.li: Pemmican for every caravan we send out, and a few packs for me.

gloomy.li: Sooner or later we'll have to run. I want something in our packs when we do.

cold.li: Pemmican keeps for months without refrigeration. That is the entire argument.

plain.li: A hundred and fifty packs of pemmican. The storeroom smells like old saddle leather.

cheerful.li: I've stacked the pemmican into a neat little wall in the storeroom. Come and see.

gloomy.li: Enough to survive on, if not to enjoy.

plain.li: We keep dragging our dead out past the fields. They deserve better, and so do the ones who have to walk past them.
[grieving] I don't want to visit a ditch to talk to them. Give them graves.

warm.li: I'd like somewhere to go and talk to the ones we've lost. Even if they can't answer.

blunt.li: I'm tired of tripping over shallow graves in the potato field. Dig real ones, with markers.

cheerful.li: Flowers, a gravel path and a bench to sit on. It could be a peaceful spot.

gloomy.li: Three graves. I'd say one for each of us who's next, but there'll be more than three.

cold.li: Bodies in the open draw scavengers. Scavengers draw hunters. Dig the graves.

plain.li: Three graves, dug and marked. It feels wrong to be glad about it, but I am.

warm.li: Someone has already left flowers on one of them.

gloomy.li: There's room for them now. We'll fill it; we always do.

plain.li: Our noble holds court in a corridor. The next imperial visitor is going to notice.

warm.li: Our noble carries a lot for the rest of us. A proper throne room is the least we can give back.

blunt.li: If I hear one more speech about proper decorum, I'm building the throne myself.

cheerful.li: A red carpet all the way to the throne, and trumpets whenever someone walks it.

gloomy.li: The Empire doesn't forgive poor hospitality, and it has a long memory.

cold.li: A satisfied noble brings imperial favor. A throne room is the price of entry.

plain.li: The throne room is done. It's very grand. I feel underdressed walking past it.

blunt.li: There. A chair for sitting importantly in. Happy now?

cheerful.li: I sat on the throne for one second! Don't tell anyone.

plain.li: The kids learn whatever the nearest grown-up knows, and sometimes that's the cook. Let's give them proper desks.

warm.li: I want the children to learn things that have nothing to do with surviving, too.

blunt.li: The kids know eleven words for raider and none for please. Fix that.

cheerful.li: Little faces at little desks, trying to look like they're paying attention. I can't wait.

gloomy.li: We won't be here forever. Somebody has to know how to keep this place going.

cold.li: A child we teach now will still be working for us when the rest of us have slowed down.

plain.li: Three desks. The children complained immediately, which means it's working.

warm.li: One of the kids read me a whole sentence today. A whole sentence.

cold.li: The children will be useful sooner now.

plain.li: Every caravan that leaves here thinks better or worse of us than when it came. Let's make it better.

warm.li: The next time a caravan limps in hungry, let's feed them and send them off with extra.

blunt.li: Somewhere out there is a faction with more guns than sense. I'd like them on our side.

cheerful.li: Traders who stay for supper, and neighbors who wave instead of shooting.

gloomy.li: Every faction out there has a reason to raid us, and not one of them has a reason to help.

cold.li: Goodwill costs silver now and saves lives later. I like that exchange.

plain.li: Their last caravan brought us a gift. I didn't know what to say.

cold.li: We now have somewhere to send our problems.

plain.li: Just once I'd like to sit on a chair that somebody cared about while making it.

warm.li: Let's give this place a few things that will outlast us.

blunt.li: Everything here looks like it was built during a raid. Mostly because it was.

cheerful.li: Two beautiful things to start with, then four, then a museum!

gloomy.li: Most days I can't tell if anything we do matters. A well-made thing would.

cold.li: Shoddy goods sell as firewood. I'd like us to stop making firewood.

blunt.li: Finally, something in this colony that doesn't wobble.

gloomy.li: Two good things, and now the raiders will want them.

plain.li: I've made a hundred things that were fine. I'd like to make one that's perfect.

warm.li: I want to make something visitors ask about. Then I can tell them all of us made it.

blunt.li: I'm wasting my hands on chairs and coats. Let me make something worth stealing.

cheerful.li: I've dreamed about it three nights running. I just need the material, the time and a bit of luck.

gloomy.li: Inspiration comes once in a while, and it never stays. If it comes, I want to be ready.

cold.li: Traders judge us by the best thing we've made. A masterwork shows them what we can do.

plain.li: People keep finding reasons to walk past it. I keep catching them.

blunt.li: Took long enough. Don't tell anyone I said it was worth it.

plain.li: Every log we cut now is one we don't have to dig out of the snow later.

warm.li: Whoever's on night watch should have a fire to come back to.

blunt.li: Trees don't cut themselves, and the cold doesn't care how tired you are.

cheerful.li: A woodpile so high we'll need a ladder to reach the top!

gloomy.li: The last thing you burn is your bed. I've heard of colonies that got that far.

cold.li: Running out of fuel in midwinter is a predictable failure. Let's not have it.

plain.li: It smells like sap and sawdust out by the woodpile.

gloomy.li: Three hundred logs. Feels like a lot, until the snow comes.
